text: The length of the statutory notice period is a versioned reference row read by product group and notice type, and its value is not fixed by any source read for this key; the same holds for the warning threshold of R-UNI-31 behind MSG-S4-002. The story computes the expiry as delivered_at plus that length and never writes a number of days in code or in the contract.
why: R-LIT-07 gives its timing column as the words notice period by product and type and R-UNI-31 says only that a threshold is reached; TSD S4 and FSD S4 give no value, so any number chosen here would be an invented business value.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-07 timing column, R-UNI-31); FSD S4 A2.3.3.1 (VR-S4-003-1, BR-S4-003); TSD S4 T4; Template and Rules section R7.2 (s17).
confirm: Business lead of S4 and the owner of the reference data
impact: If the business fixes a length per product group and notice type, only the reference rows change; the timer, the shapes and the tests do not.

text: The proof window of R-LIT-08 is 7 days and it runs from the dispatch date the notice record holds, which is the date the notice was sent; when the notice read returns no dispatch date the window is measured from the approved_at of the approval of API-S4-001. A result of refused, returned or undeliverable is treated with R-LIT-08 for the state move and with R-LIT-09 for the alternate service notice to rwb-comms.
why: R-LIT-08 gives 7 days as its timing but no start instant, and R-LIT-09 covers three further results without saying whether they consume the same window; a window with no start cannot be tested and cannot be built.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09); FSD S4 A2.2.3.1; TSD S4 T4 (R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09); Temporal design slide 7 (the proof window is 7 days).
confirm: Business lead of S4 and the litigation officer role
impact: If the window starts on a different fact, one line of the validator changes and the test data of TC-E5-003-03 is re-dated; no shape changes.

text: The notice period is a durable timer of the LitigationWorkflow stage on task queue rwb-litigation, held in the workflow state with started_at, expires_at, the reference length, the rule ID and its version. It is not a Quartz job, not a Temporal Schedule and not a row: S4 owns no timer table, and the timer ledger of DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 is rwb-case's. DP-10 is therefore not applied and no RWB-PLT-E1071-CON row is added.
why: FSD S4 A2.3.2 names a Quartz scheduler and the legacy data block names a timer table, while the ownership rows give S4 only hearing and legal_action and Architecture v5 slide 10 gives the case service the timers; a period of one case is also not a calendar, so a Schedule would fire for the wrong object.
read: FSD S4 A2.3.2; legacy RWB-E5-003 data block (timer, DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036); context pack ownership rows (S4 tables: hearing, legal_action; workflows: LitigationWorkflow); Architecture v5 slide 10; Template and Rules section R5.5 (DP-10).
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of the workflow platform
impact: If the platform insists on a Schedule or a timer table, a row is added to the service schema and a Schedule is registered; the rule answers and the shapes stay as published.

text: The three case states of the rules — WITH_CUSTOMER_NOTICE_PERIOD, NOTICE_UNSERVED and PACK_ASSEMBLY — are states of the case of record, so this service announces the route fact with the rule ID and its version on the case contract of rwb-case and accepts the answer; it writes no recovery_case row and evaluates no case rule.
why: The three rules name the case as the object that moves and the case is P3's, while this service's own status list has no value that names a notice period; writing the case row here would break DP-01 and the case of record.
read: TSD S4 T4 (R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-15); FSD S4 A2.3.3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; context pack (S4 owns hearing and legal_action); Architecture v5 slide 41.
confirm: Owner of rwb-case and the business lead of S4
impact: If the case contract exposes one operation per state instead of a route fact with a rule, the client maps three calls instead of one; the decision records and the timer do not change.

text: The notice record, its template, its state and its served result are rwb-comms's (P6) and are read or announced on its contract; this service writes no notice row, although the Ownership Map gives S4 the approve operation on a notice and the FSD says the delivery confirmation is written onto the notice.
why: The Ownership Map gives S4 the tables hearing and legal_action only, Architecture v5 slide 10 assigns notices to rwb-comms, and DP-01 forbids writing another service's table; the approve operation stays here because the Ownership Map and TSD S4 T-A.1 publish it as this service's.
read: Context pack ownership rows (S4 tables, five operations including POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve); Architecture v5 slide 10 (Notices, rwb-comms); FSD S4 A2.2.2 and A2.2.3.1; TSD S4 T3.1 (no notice table) and T-A.1 (API-S4-001).
confirm: Owner of rwb-comms and the owner of the Ownership Map
impact: If the notice table turns out to be S4's, a notice DDL template and a notice sub-resource are added at major version 1 and the served result is written here; the served result of a delivered notice and the period do not change.

text: The proof of delivery is a document of rwb-document: this service asks for the attach of the WIN proof to the notice and keeps the returned proof reference as the inputs reference of the decision record; the document, its custody in DMS and its retention are the hub's, and no document row is written here.
why: R-LIT-07 names WIN and DMS as its systems, the document hub is P5's by Architecture v5 slide 8, and the Ownership Map gives S4 no document table; storing a copy here would duplicate custody and bring personal data into this schema.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-07 systems column); FSD S4 A2.2.3.1; TSD S4 T5.2 (P5 for documents); context pack ownership rows.
impact: If the hub exposes an attach that also returns the delivered date, the validator reads it from there instead of the notice read; nothing else changes.

text: This story publishes no Kafka event and consumes none: the Ownership Map gives S4 zero events and DP-09 is not in the story's pattern set, so the WIN delivery result reaches the litigation stage as the noticeDeliveryResult signal, and the case fact leaves on the case contract. Architecture v5 slide 19 shows NoticeDelivered as an input of rwb-litigation; whether that event exists and who consumes it stays open.
why: A consumer without a DP-09 platform row would need an inbox, an idempotency table and a retry policy that no story of this key owns, and a producer would add an event the ownership rows do not carry.
read: Context pack ownership rows (S4 events: none); Architecture v5 slide 19 (inputs NoticeDelivered, PartnerResultSubmitted); Template and Rules section R5.5 (DP-09).
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of the event platform
impact: If NoticeDelivered becomes a topic of rwb-comms, a consumer, an inbox and a DP-09 platform dependency are added and the signal keeps its shape as the body of the event.

text: The approval of a notice for dispatch is a person's approval at Litigation right A, and where the case, the amount or the product puts it above the officer's own authority it is routed through the approval contract of rwb-decision; the delegation table, the level and the approval clock are rwb-decision's and the role codes that hold right A are those of the legacy permission block and TSD S4 T6.1.
why: Architecture v5 slide 3 states that every decision is approved within authority and recorded by rwb-decision, while the FSD names the approval as a user right and no source gives this service a delegation table; re-implementing the table here would fork the authority model.
read: Architecture v5 slide 3 (approvals within authority, P7); FSD S4 A2.3.3.3; legacy RWB-E5-003 permission block (Litigation A: RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-HEADLIT); TSD S4 T6.1; Template and Rules section R5.5 (DP-08 not applied).
confirm: Owner of rwb-decision and the Head of Litigation role
impact: If the approval is always local to the right holder, the client is removed and the operation answers from the permission of the caller; the decision record and the task are unchanged.

text: The four operations this service calls — the notice read and unserved announcement of rwb-comms, the proof attach of rwb-document, the case read and route fact of rwb-case and the approval route of rwb-decision — have no published name and no published answer field list in any source read for this key, so the app and the contract carry the placeholder and are built against the fakes.
why: No source read for this key names those operations, and inventing a path would fix a shape its owner has not agreed; the story must still name the hand-over so that the drift test has something to compare.
read: TSD S4 T5.2 (calls through published interfaces, no operation names); FSD S4 A2.3.2 integration points; context pack ownership rows (S4 provides five operations and consumes none by name); legacy RWB-E5-003 endpoints block.
confirm: Owners of rwb-comms, rwb-document, rwb-case and rwb-decision
impact: Each confirmed operation replaces a placeholder row in 12.2 and one fake; no rule, timer or element of the resource changes.

text: The notice period is published as an element of the noticeDeliveryResult signal and of the read answer of the legal action, and never as a column of legal_action and never as a Schedule. The element carries startedAt, expiresAt, periodLengthRef, ruleId and ruleVersion, and the length itself stays a reference.
why: TSD S4 T3.1 gives no period or delivered_at field and the Ownership Map gives S4 no timer table, while a Schedule cannot belong to one case; the period must still be readable by the two screens and testable by the drift test.
read: TSD S4 T3.1 (DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014, no period field), T3.0; Architecture v5 slide 10 (timers of rwb-case); Template and Rules section R5.5 (DP-10, DP-15).
confirm: Solution architect and the tech lead of rwb-litigation
impact: If a period row is required for reporting, a legal_action extension column or a period table is added as a new major version and the reporting read model takes it from the events of the service.

text: The index set of legal_action beyond the primary key on id is not declared by any source read for this key, so the DDL template declares the primary key only; the app story names the two lookups it needs, by case_id and by id, and adds no index beyond what the template declares.
why: A guessed index would be a migration the owners never agreed and would have to be dropped when the real set arrives; the two lookups are the only access paths this key needs.
read: TSD S4 T3.1 (columns and types, no index block); TSD S4 T-A.1 (the paths that read a legal action); Template and Rules section R5.5 (DP-15).
confirm: Data steward and the ACE DB team
impact: When the index set is published the template gains it in a new migration; no API and no rule changes.

text: The legacy master and the Epics 3 to 8 specification carry no requirement identifier for this feature, so both slices trace to FEAT-LIT-03 until the PRD adds them; the business text of the 409 of a notice that is not NOTICE_DISPATCHED and the code of the 400 are also unstated, so the contract publishes the status, its causes and the messageId slot and no text.
why: No source read for this key gives a REQ identifier, a 409 message text or a 400 code, and inventing one would put a value in the traceability and in the error model that no owner backs.
read: TSD S4 T8 (requirement table, FEAT-LIT-01 only); FSD S4 A2.3.4; legacy RWB-E5-003 acceptance criteria and messages; TSD S4 T-A.2 (error statuses, no texts); Template and Rules section R7.2 (s14).
confirm: Business analyst of S4 and the owner of the message catalogue
impact: The PRD adds the REQ identifiers and the catalogue adds the two texts; the story files gain rows and no behaviour changes.
